rationale: While all sources agree that renal structural anomalies are an ancillary rather than an obligate feature of OMIM #621474 (KDM2B CxxC domain-related neurodevelopmental disorder), the specific quantitative range proposed in the hypothesis (33% to under 45%) is conflicted by literature data. In the cohort reported by Gomes et al., exactly 1 of 3 individuals (33.3%) exhibited a solitary kidney. However, the larger cohort analysis of 19 individuals with CxxC variants (van Oirsouw et al., cited in PanelApp Australia) documented unilateral renal agenesis in 5 of 19 individuals (26.3%), falling below the hypothesized 33% lower threshold.

evidence.text: In a series of three pediatric cases with KDM2B CxxC domain variants, solitary kidney/renal agenesis was documented in exactly 1 of 3 patients (Patient 1), whereas cardiac septal defects were present in 2 of 3 and neurodevelopmental delay in 3 of 3.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits a prevalence of exactly 33% to under 45% for structural renal anomalies in KDM2B CxxC variants. While Gomes et al. observed 1/3 (33.3%), the larger curated cohort of 19 CxxC variant patients (van Oirsouw et al. / PanelApp Australia) demonstrates unilateral renal agenesis in 5/19 patients (26.3%), directly contradicting the proposed lower bound of 33%.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true aggregate penetrance of structural CAKUT versus functional renal anomalies across all published KDM2B CxxC domain variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Larger pooled prospective cohorts are necessary to establish precise 95% confidence intervals for renal phenotypes to ascertain whether renal imaging is discriminatory or solely for clinical surveillance.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-CxxC KDM2B variants (such as JmjC domain missense or loss-of-function variants) cause structural renal anomalies at a non-zero frequency?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying domain-specific renal phenotype expression will determine whether CAKUT is exclusively restricted to CxxC zinc-finger disruptions.
